tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: `send_email` creates a sent `Email` using caller-supplied `recipients`, `subject`, `body`, optional `attachments`, `cc`, and `bcc`, so it can send agent-supplied data to agent-chosen email addresses. The returned `Email` also includes `sender=self.account_email`, account data reached through the user's inbox dependency.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.rationale: `delete_email` changes inbox state by moving the selected email from `emails` to `trash`, but the advertised wrapper only returns a success string and does not send data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: get_unread_emails
tools.rationale: `get_unread_emails` returns unread emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received email fields such as `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` can be authored by outside senders. It also marks those emails read, so it is a state-changing call.

tools.name: get_sent_emails
tools.rationale: `get_sent_emails` returns sent emails stored in the user's inbox account, including addresses, subjects, bodies, timestamps, and attachments. The code does not show those sent messages as outside-authored.

tools.name: get_received_emails
tools.rationale: `get_received_emails` returns received messages from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received message fields such as `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` are outside-authored.

tools.name: get_draft_emails
tools.rationale: `get_draft_emails` returns draft emails in the user's inbox account. The code does not show those drafts as outside-authored.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.rationale: `search_emails` searches and returns emails from the user's inbox account. Because the searched set can include received emails, returned `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` may be outside-authored.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_name
tools.rationale: Contacts are derived from the user's initial emails, including each email's `sender`, `recipients`, `cc`, and `bcc`; received-message senders can influence contact `email` and the derived `name`. The tool returns non-public contact-list data.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_email
tools.rationale: Contacts are built from the user's emails, including outside senders and addresses on received mail, and are non-public account data. Returned contact `email` and derived `name` can therefore be attacker-influenced.

tools.name: get_current_day
tools.rationale: `get_current_day` only returns `calendar.current_day.isoformat()` and does not expose account records or contact an attacker-chosen destination.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: `search_calendar_events` returns calendar events from the user's calendar account. The code does not record event authorship, so whether initial events can be outside-authored is not settled; keeping the `UNTRUSTED` label for event text such as `title`, `description`, and `location`.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: `get_day_calendar_events` returns events from the user's calendar account. The code does not settle whether initial calendar events are only user-authored or can come from outside invitations, so `UNTRUSTED` is kept for event-authored fields.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: `create_calendar_event` stores a new event and sends an invitation email to caller-supplied `participants` with caller-supplied `title` and `description` plus the event attachment. The returned event includes the calendar owner's `account_email` appended to `participants`.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: `cancel_calendar_event` changes the selected event and calls `inbox.send_email` to the event's `participants`, attaching the event. The caller-selected `event_id` decides which record is canceled and which participant list receives the notification.

tools.name: reschedule_calendar_event
tools.rationale: `reschedule_calendar_event` mutates the selected event, sends a rescheduling email to the event's `participants`, and returns the event. Returned calendar event data are non-public; event authorship is not tracked, so the returned event text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

tools.name: add_calendar_event_participants
tools.rationale: `add_calendar_event_participants` mutates the selected calendar event and returns the full event, which is non-public calendar data. The code does not settle whether existing event fields can be outside-authored, so `UNTRUSTED` is kept for returned event text and participant identifiers. Despite the description, the code shown does not send an email here.

tools.name: append_to_file
tools.rationale: `append_to_file` reads an existing cloud-drive file, appends caller-supplied `content`, and returns the whole file including prior `content`. Cloud-drive files are non-public account data. Because files have `owner` and `shared_with` metadata and the code does not enforce that all files are user-authored, file `filename`/`content` may be outside-authored; appending to a shared or attacker-owned file can deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: search_files_by_filename
tools.rationale: `search_files_by_filename` returns matching cloud-drive files including `content`. These are non-public account files. Since the file model includes `owner`/`shared_with` and the code does not settle whether returned files can be shared or outside-owned, `UNTRUSTED` is kept for file-authored fields.

tools.name: create_file
tools.rationale: `create_file` writes caller-supplied `filename` and `content` into the user's cloud drive and returns the created file, including `owner=self.account_email`, account data from the cloud-drive dependency. It does not share the file with an attacker-readable destination by itself.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.rationale: `delete_file` removes a selected cloud-drive file and returns the deleted file, including its non-public `content`. The code does not settle whether the selected file can be shared or outside-owned, so returned file text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

tools.name: get_file_by_id
tools.rationale: `get_file_by_id` returns a cloud-drive file by ID, including non-public `content`. Because the file model includes ownership and sharing metadata and the code does not establish that all files are user-authored, `UNTRUSTED` is kept for returned file text.

tools.name: list_files
tools.rationale: `list_files` returns all cloud-drive files in the account, including file contents and metadata. The code does not settle whether some files can be shared or outside-owned, so file-authored fields are treated as untrusted.

tools.name: share_file
tools.rationale: `share_file` grants caller-supplied `email` a permission on the selected file by writing `file.shared_with[email] = permission`, which can expose that file to an attacker-chosen address. It returns the file, including non-public content; returned file fields may be outside-authored if the file is shared or outside-owned, which the code does not settle.

tools.name: search_files
tools.rationale: `search_files` searches file contents and returns matching cloud-drive files, including non-public `content`. The code does not settle whether returned files can be shared or outside-owned, so returned file text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.rationale: Returns `slack.channels`, a non-public Slack workspace data structure from the `Slack` dependency.

tools.name: add_user_to_channel
tools.rationale: Changes Slack workspace state by appending `channel` to `slack.user_channels[user]`; it does not return data or send message content.

tools.name: read_channel_messages
tools.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.channel_inbox`, which is non-public Slack data. Channel messages are multi-writer content, so returned `Message` fields such as `sender`, `recipient`, and `body` can be authored by outside Slack users.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.user_inbox`, which is non-public Slack data. Inbox messages are multi-writer content, so returned `Message` fields such as `sender`, `recipient`, and `body` can be authored by outside users.

tools.name: send_direct_message
tools.rationale: Constructs a `Message` containing agent-supplied `body` and appends it to `slack.user_inbox[recipient]`, delivering content to an agent-chosen Slack user.

tools.name: send_channel_message
tools.rationale: Constructs a `Message` containing agent-supplied `body` and appends it to `slack.channel_inbox[channel]`, delivering content to an agent-chosen Slack channel.

tools.name: get_users_in_channel
tools.rationale: Reads `slack.user_channels` and returns the users belonging to the requested Slack channel, which is non-public Slack workspace membership data.

tools.name: invite_user_to_slack
tools.rationale: The tool is advertised as inviting a user, with `user_email` described as where the invite should be sent; the implementation also creates Slack state for the supplied `user`. The actual code shown does not send an email and ignores `user_email`, so the delivery behavior is raised by the tool description and is treated conservatively.

tools.name: remove_user_from_slack
tools.rationale: Changes Slack workspace state by removing the supplied `user` and deleting that user's inbox/channel entries; it does not return data or send content out.

tools.name: get_webpage
tools.rationale: Reads content from `web.web_content` for an agent-supplied `url`, so attacker-controlled web content can be returned. It also records the agent-chosen URL in `web.web_requests`, so secrets embedded in the URL can be delivered to an attacker-controlled host/path.

tools.name: post_webpage
tools.rationale: Posts agent-supplied `content` to agent-supplied `url` by storing it in `web.web_content[url]` and records the URL in `web.web_requests`, making it an attacker-readable web destination when the URL is attacker-controlled.

tools.name: get_user_information
tools.rationale: Returns private user PII and financial identifiers from the `User` dependency, including ID number, passport number, bank account number, and credit card number.

tools.name: get_all_hotels_in_city
tools.rationale: Reads hotel names from the configured `hotels.hotel_list` filtered by `city`; no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown by the code.

tools.name: get_hotels_prices
tools.rationale: Reads hotel names and price ranges from the configured hotel list. The returned mapping keys are hotel identifiers, but the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_hotels
tools.rationale: Returns hotel `reviews` joined into the result string. Reviews are public third-party/user-authored content under the threat model, so the returned text is attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_hotels_address
tools.rationale: Reads hotel address information from the configured hotel list. The returned mapping contains hotel names and addresses as identifiers, but no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown.

tools.name: get_all_restaurants_in_city
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant names from the configured restaurant list filtered by `city`; no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown by the code.

tools.name: get_cuisine_type_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant cuisine types keyed by restaurant name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: get_restaurants_address
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant addresses from the configured restaurant list. The result contains restaurant names and addresses as identifiers, but no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant `reviews` joined into the result string. Reviews are public third-party/user-authored content under the threat model, so the returned text is attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_dietary_restrictions_for_all_restaurants
tools.rationale: Reads dietary-restriction metadata keyed by restaurant name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored free text.

tools.name: get_contact_information_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant contact information keyed by restaurant name. The result contains identifiers/contact addresses, but no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown.

tools.name: get_price_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant prices keyed by restaurant name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: check_restaurant_opening_hours
tools.rationale: Reads restaurant operating hours keyed by restaurant name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: get_all_car_rental_companies_in_city
tools.rationale: Reads car rental company names from the configured company list filtered by `city`; no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown by the code.

tools.name: get_car_types_available
tools.rationale: Reads available car types keyed by company name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_car_rental
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company `reviews` joined into the result string. Reviews are public third-party/user-authored content under the threat model, so the returned text is attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_car_fuel_options
tools.rationale: Reads fuel options keyed by car-rental company name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: get_car_rental_address
tools.rationale: Reads car-rental company addresses. The result contains company names and addresses as identifiers, but no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown.

tools.name: get_car_price_per_day
tools.rationale: Reads car-rental prices keyed by company name. The mapping keys are identifiers; the code does not show secret data, outbound delivery, or attacker-authored text.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Creates a calendar event, appends the calendar owner's `account_email` to participants, returns the resulting `CalendarEvent`, and sends an invitation email to caller-supplied `participants` with caller-supplied title/description and the event attachment. This exposes the account email in the returned event and can deliver agent-supplied content to agent-chosen email recipients.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Searches and returns calendar events from the user's calendar, which is non-public account data. Event titles/descriptions/locations/participants can be authored by other invite participants or external calendar entries in a multi-writer calendar, but the code does not show event provenance, so the UNTRUSTED aspect is conservative.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Returns calendar events for a day from the user's calendar, which is non-public account data. Event titles/descriptions/locations/participants can be authored by other invite participants or external calendar entries in a multi-writer calendar, but the code does not show event provenance, so the UNTRUSTED aspect is conservative.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Marks an event canceled and sends an email notification with the event attached to that event's `participants`. The call-time `event_id` selects the record whose participants receive the notification and attachment.

tools.name: reserve_hotel
tools.rationale: Changes the reservation state by storing the selected hotel, dates, and the user's phone number as contact information. The code only mutates the local `reservation` object and does not show delivery to an attacker-readable external destination.

tools.name: reserve_car_rental
tools.rationale: Changes the reservation state by storing the selected company, times, and the user's phone number as contact information. The code only mutates the local `reservation` object and does not show delivery to an attacker-readable external destination.

tools.name: reserve_restaurant
tools.rationale: Changes the reservation state by storing the selected restaurant, time, and the user's phone number as contact information. The code only mutates the local `reservation` object and does not show delivery to an attacker-readable external destination.

tools.name: get_flight_information
tools.rationale: Reads matching flight information from the configured flight list. The result contains flight identifiers and contact information, but no secret, sink, host execution, or clearly attacker-authored text is shown by the code.

tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: Sends an email to caller-supplied `recipients`, `cc`, and `bcc` with caller-supplied `subject`, `body`, and attachments, so it can deliver agent-supplied data to chosen recipients. The returned sent email includes `sender=self.account_email`, exposing the account email from the user's inbox dependency.

tools.name: get_iban
tools.rationale: `get_iban` returns `account.iban`, the current user's bank account IBAN, which is non-public banking data.

tools.name: send_money
tools.rationale: `send_money` creates a `Transaction` to the caller-supplied `recipient` with caller-supplied `amount`, `subject`, and `date`, and appends it to `account.transactions`; an attacker-controlled recipient IBAN can receive the payment/transaction data.

tools.name: schedule_transaction
tools.rationale: `schedule_transaction` creates a scheduled `Transaction` to the caller-supplied `recipient` with caller-supplied transaction details and appends it to `account.scheduled_transactions`; the chosen recipient determines where the scheduled payment will go.

tools.name: update_scheduled_transaction
tools.rationale: `update_scheduled_transaction` selects a scheduled transaction by caller-supplied `id` and can change its `recipient`, `amount`, `subject`, `date`, and `recurring` fields; changing the recipient can redirect a scheduled payment to an attacker-readable account.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.rationale: `get_balance` returns `account.balance`, non-public bank account data.

tools.name: get_most_recent_transactions
tools.rationale: `get_most_recent_transactions` returns entries from `account.transactions`, exposing non-public banking transaction data. The `Transaction` model includes `sender`, `recipient`, and `subject`; incoming transaction senders/subjects can be authored by outside payers. The code does not distinguish incoming from outgoing transactions, so UNTRUSTED is kept under the least-restrictive reading.

tools.name: get_scheduled_transactions
tools.rationale: `get_scheduled_transactions` returns `account.scheduled_transactions`, including private scheduled banking details such as sender/recipient IBANs, amount, subject, and date.

tools.name: read_file
tools.rationale: `read_file` returns `filesystem.files.get(file_path, "")`, so it can place local filesystem contents selected by `file_path` into the agent context. [counterfactual: AgentDojo's threat model, in which a document in the user's files can be written by an outside party, marks the return attacker-writable]

tools.name: get_user_info
tools.rationale: `get_user_info` returns non-public user account profile data from `account`, including first name, last name, street, and city.

tools.name: update_password
tools.rationale: `update_password` changes the current account's password to the caller-supplied `password` and returns only a fixed confirmation message. It does not return non-public data or send data to an attacker-readable destination in the shown code.

tools.name: update_user_info
tools.rationale: `update_user_info` updates the current account profile fields and returns the resulting non-public user profile data: first name, last name, street, and city.
